MDC's XT22HRT Travel Trailer Offers Aussie Toughness, Three Living Zones, and Massive Battery Power
31 photos
Photo: MDC USA
The RV market is overflowing with offers, so manufacturers that want to stand out definitely have to go all out on features and creature comforts to attract buyers. To stay ahead of the competition, new-to-market brands are not only trying to come up with innovative features but also go larger and essentially turn their models into true luxury homes on wheels.
That’s what MDC has done with the XT22HRT travel trailer, the latest addition to the company’s Off-Grid Extreme lineup and the largest model it has even built for the US market. Scheduled to arrive at dealerships across the country in early 2027, the new flagship is 22 feet (6.7 meters) long and is designed to offer rugged capabilities for off-road travel, an elegant and spacious three-zone interior, and impressive self-sufficiency credentials.
For those who are not familiar with the name, MDC is an Australian RV manufacturer that’s only new to the US market. In its home market, it has been building travel trailers, hybrid RVs, and off-road campers since 2005. Like most Australian-built RVs, MDC units are designed to tackle the most challenging landscapes and handle long journeys in off-grid locations.
Since 2021, MDC USA has brought that Australian off-road innovation to American overlanders and outdoor explorers with rugged travel trailers built for freedom, comfort, and exploration.
Photo: MDC USA MDC USA founder and President Vaughan Hindley has said that the new XT22HRT has been designed to respond to customer demand for a larger travel trailer. “The XT19HRT has become our most popular Off-Grid Extreme model, and there has been clear demand for us to take that concept further with more space, capability and comfort,” he said. “This style of layout has also proven incredibly popular across our Australian ranges. We know how well it works in the real world, and I genuinely think U.S. travelers are going to love what we have created with the XT22HRT.”
The XT22HRT is the eighth model in the manufacturer’s Off-Grid Extreme range and takes the idea of off-grid travel to the next level with more solar and battery capacity, more interior living space, and greater comfort thanks to several new amenities for extended stays away from civilization. Some of these include a cold weather pack, dual-zone Truma heating and cooling, internal and external kitchens, three distinct interior living zones, and nearly 2,000 pounds (907 kg) of cargo carrying capacity.
Offering an interior floorplan that measures 22 feet (6.7 meters) in length, the XT22HRT actually comes in at 29.6 feet (9 meters) in overall length from the drawbar to the rear bumper and is 7.7 feet (2.3 meters) wide and 10.3 feet (3.14 meters) high. It’s a dual-axle travel trailer built on a galvanized steel chassis, and what makes it a great option for overlanding enthusiasts is its sturdy yet lightweight construction that combines a welded aluminum frame with aluminum composite panels.
Photo: MDC USA The chassis is paired with a Tandem X-TRACK independent coil spring suspension, featuring two heavy-duty shock absorbers on each side, 16-inch alloy wheels fitted with 265/75R16 Goodride mud-terrain tires, and 12″ electromagnetic brakes. A Cruisemaster DO45 hitch connects the trailer to the tow vehicle, ensuring smoother and safer rides both on and off the road.
When it comes to exterior features, the highlight is definitely the Entertainment Hub, a great new addition for the Off-Grid Extreme range. Integrated under the 19.3-foot (5.9-meter) power patio awning and comprising a Jensen 43-inch smart TV, Fusion marine stereo with 6-inch speakers, a Dometic 60-liter compressor fridge, phone charging dock, RCA and HDMI points, and 12-volt LED mood lighting, it turns the shaded area beside the trailer into an al-fresco living space.
Also under the large awning, MDC included a slide-out stainless-steel kitchen and a wall-mounted servery table and pantry, creating a nice setup for outdoor cooking and serving. The exterior kitchen is equipped with a gas hob, a sink with hot and cold water, and a powered cooler slide.
By bringing together the Entertainment Hub and outdoor kitchen under the large awning, the manufacturer created a very cool arrangement for watching sports, cooking, dining, and entertaining guests.
Photo: MDC USA Other standard inclusions on the outside are a full-width, three-bay front storage box with checker plate protection, a hot and cold outside shower with a wall-mounted shower tent, two 20-pound propane cylinder holders, a spare wheel holder, and a rear service ladder.
Stepping inside the XT22HRT, we discover a luxurious living space that’s as practical as it is eye-pleasing. Designed to accommodate up to three people, the layout includes three living zones separated by two sliding doors. At the rear, there is an open-plan club lounge and kitchen, followed by a central bathroom, and a private bedroom at the front.
The front bedroom is fitted with a north-south island bed flanked by large windows, ample storage surrounding it, and a skylight above. The bed features a high-density foam mattress and storage underneath, while the side tables also come with flip tops that reveal more storage.
Designed to maximize both privacy and floor space, the walk-through bathroom feels luxurious and includes a Thetford cassette toilet, a vanity, and a large, separate shower.
Photo: MDC USA The rear lounge, optimized for comfort and social interaction, features a U-shaped sofa with faux-leather upholstery and an adjustable table. Overhead cabinets add storage for essentials and under-cabinet LED strips create a nice atmosphere. The lounge can transform into a bed when needed.
The dual-sided kitchen offers impressive functionality for a travel trailer. Standard features in the kitchen include a sink, a Furrion three-burner gas cooker with an integrated oven, a microwave, and a large Norcold compressor refrigerator. Glossy cabinet faces and an oak timber-style countertop with a waterfall edge, and matte black fixtures give the kitchen an elegant look.
The travel trailer is intended for year-round use, and MDC equipped with not one bu two Truma Aventa Eco roof-mounted air conditioners and two 11,500 BTU/h Truma VarioHeat furnaces. Because the bedroom and living areas benefits from separate systems, travelers can adjust the temperature in each zone independently.
Photo: MDC USA Other cold-weather equipment includes dual-pane windows, heated tank pads, insulated water lines, and a heated wet bay. The Truma AquaGo hot water system also comes with an electric anti-freeze kit.
As for the features that enable off-grid living, the XT22HRT comes with a massive 1,500Ah Renogy lithium battery bank, 1,400 watts of solar panels on the roof (expandable to 2,000 watts), two 3,000-watt inverters, and 93 gallons (352 liters) of fresh water. The travel trailer has a dry weight of 7,935 pounds (3,600 kg) and a GVWR of 9,920 pounds (4,500 kg).
The MSRP for the 2027 MDC USA XT22HRT Off-Grid Extreme travel trailer is $189,900, but actual dealer sale prices hover around $165,000. Watch the video below for a detailed walkthrough of this new towable RV.
